specimenDrops.name: Martian Regolith Dust
specimenDrops.quickFact: Martian soil is rich in iron oxide (rust), giving the Red Planet its signature fiery glow.

specimenDrops.name: Basalt Regolith Crust
specimenDrops.quickFact: NASA Opportunity rover ground into surface rocks using its Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT).

specimenDrops.name: Hematite Blueberry Cluster
specimenDrops.quickFact: Hematite spherules form when liquid water percolates through porous sedimentary rock.

specimenDrops.name: Groundwater Nodule
specimenDrops.quickFact: These tiny gray spheres proved that liquid water once drenched ancient Mars!

specimenDrops.name: Permafrost Ice Core
specimenDrops.quickFact: NASA Phoenix lander scraped away topsoil to expose pure water ice that sublimated in days.

specimenDrops.name: Glacier Subsurface Shard
specimenDrops.quickFact: Mars holds enough subsurface ice to cover the entire planet in an ocean 35 meters deep!

specimenDrops.name: MOXIE Electrolysis Catalyst
specimenDrops.quickFact: MOXIE splits Martian CO2 molecules at 800°C into breathable O2 and carbon monoxide.

specimenDrops.name: Hydroponic Microgreen Sample
specimenDrops.quickFact: Astronauts on the ISS grow fresh radishes and lettuce using LED lighting and aeroponic mist.
